subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-year-old boy is evaluated for an asymptomatic abdominal mass noted by his parents. Imaging shows a large renal tumor, and he undergoes nephrectomy for Wilms tumor. His chemotherapy regimen includes actinomycin D (dactinomycin), which intercalates between DNA base pairs.
question: Which of the following best describes the effect of this drug on nucleic acid synthesis?

options.text: It selectively inhibits eukaryotic RNA polymerase II
It selectively inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase
It inhibits RNA polymerase in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes
It inhibits topoisomerase II, causing double-strand breaks
It inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, depleting deoxyribonucleotides

explanation_correct: Dactinomycin binds DNA by intercalation and inhibits RNA polymerase in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes, blocking transcription; this activity underlies its use against Wilms tumor and other cancers. Because it is not selective for a particular polymerase, it is highly toxic. Its action is distinct from alpha-amanitin, which selectively inhibits eukaryotic RNA polymerase II, and from rifampin, which inhibits the bacterial enzyme.

explanation_incorrect.A: Alpha-amanitin selectively inhibits eukaryotic RNA polymerase II; dactinomycin inhibits RNA polymerase in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.
explanation_incorrect.B: Rifampin selectively inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
explanation_incorrect.D: Topoisomerase II inhibitors such as etoposide cause double-strand breaks; dactinomycin acts by intercalation and transcriptional inhibition.
explanation_incorrect.E: Ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited by hydroxyurea, not by dactinomycin.

educationalObjective: Dactinomycin intercalates into DNA and inhibits RNA polymerase in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes, blocking transcription.
